label: Matt 21:1
text: When they came near to Jerusalem, and came to Bethsphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,

label: Matt 21:2
text:
saying to them,
“Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them, and bring them to me.

label: Matt 21:3
text: If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord needs them,’ and immediately he will send them.”

label: Matt 21:4
text: All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,

label: Matt 21:5
text:
“Tell the daughter of Zion,
behold, your King comes to you,
humble, and riding on a donkey,
on a colt, the foal of a donkey.”

label: Matt 21:6
text: The disciples went, and did just as Jesus commanded them,

label: Matt 21:7
text: and brought the donkey and the colt, and laid their clothes on them; and he sat on them.

label: Matt 21:8
text: A very great multitude spread their clothes on the road. Others cut branches from the trees, and spread them on the road.

label: Matt 21:9
text:
The multitudes who went in front of him, and those who followed, kept shouting, “Hosanna
 to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

label: Matt 21:10
text: When he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”

label: Matt 21:11
text: The multitudes said, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”

label: Matt 21:12
text: Jesus entered into the temple of God, and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.

label: Matt 21:13
text:
He said to them,
“It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’
but you have made it a den of robbers!”

label: Matt 21:14
text: The blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

label: Matt 21:15
text: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children who were crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the son of David!” they were indignant,

label: Matt 21:16
text:
and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?”
Jesus said to them,
“Yes. Did you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of babes and nursing babies you have perfected praise?’”

label: Matt 21:17
text: He left them, and went out of the city to Bethany, and camped there.

label: Matt 21:18
text: Now in the morning, as he returned to the city, he was hungry.

label: Matt 21:19
text:
Seeing a fig tree by the road, he came to it, and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it,
“Let there be no fruit from you forever!”

Immediately the fig tree withered away.

label: Matt 21:20
text: When the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree immediately wither away?”

label: Matt 21:21
text:
Jesus answered them,
“Most certainly I tell you, if you have faith, and don’t doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you told this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it would be done.

label: Matt 21:22
text: All things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”

label: Matt 21:23
text: When he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?”

label: Matt 21:24
text:
Jesus answered them,
“I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.

label: Matt 21:25
text:
The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?”

They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

label: Matt 21:26
text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.”

label: Matt 21:27
text:
They answered Jesus, and said, “We don’t know.”
He also said to them,
“Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.

label: Matt 21:28
text: But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’

label: Matt 21:29
text: He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went.

label: Matt 21:30
text: He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’ m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go.

label: Matt 21:31
text:
Which of the two did the will of his father?”
They said to him, “The first.”
Jesus said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God’s Kingdom before you.

label: Matt 21:32
text: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.

label: Matt 21:33
text: “Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household, who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and went into another country.

label: Matt 21:34
text: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers, to receive his fruit.

label: Matt 21:35
text: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.

label: Matt 21:36
text: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they treated them the same way.

label: Matt 21:37
text: But afterward he sent to them his son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

label: Matt 21:38
text: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and seize his inheritance.’

label: Matt 21:39
text: So they took him, and threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.

label: Matt 21:40
text: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”

label: Matt 21:41
text: They told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers, who will give him the fruit in its season.”

label: Matt 21:42
text:
Jesus said to them,
“Did you never read in the Scriptures,

‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the head of the corner.
This was from the Lord.
It is marvelous in our eyes?’

label: Matt 21:43
text: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you, and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.

label: Matt 21:44
text: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”

label: Matt 21:45
text: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke about them.

label: Matt 21:46
text: When they sought to seize him, they feared the multitudes, because they considered him to be a prophet.

label: Bethphage
note: 'house of unripe figs' (Imperial Aramaic), per the fetched Wikipedia article

label: Jesus approaches Jerusalem via Bethphage and the Mount of Olives
statement: Jesus approached Jerusalem from Jericho and came to Bethsphage, at the Mount of Olives, and sent two disciples into the village opposite.

label: Disciples fetch a donkey and its colt
statement: The disciples found, untied and brought a donkey tied with its colt, saying 'The Lord needs them' if questioned.

label: The entry quoted with Zechariah 9:9 (donkey and colt)
statement: The entry is narrated with the words of Zechariah 9:9 (a quotation in the text): 'your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey'.

label: Garments laid on the animals as a mount
statement: Garments were laid on the animals to serve as a riding cushion for the royal entry.

label: Crowd spreads cloaks and branches on the road
statement: A great crowd spread clothes and cut branches on the road ahead of him, an honorific welcome of a royal or victorious entrant.

label: The crowd acclaims 'Hosanna to the son of David' (Psalm 118)
statement: The crowds acclaimed him with 'Hosanna to the son of David' and 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord', the language of Psalm 118:25-26.

label: All the city is stirred; the crowd names Jesus of Nazareth a prophet
statement: His arrival stirred the whole city, and the crowds identified him as 'the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee'.

label: Jesus drives out sellers and buyers in the Temple courts
statement: Jesus entered the Temple courts and drove out all who sold and bought there.

label: Money changers exchanged coin for the half-shekel Temple tax
statement: Money changers operated in and for the Temple, exchanging pilgrims' currency for the half-shekel Temple tax, which was required to be Tyrian silver.

label: Doves sold in the Temple for purification offerings
statement: Doves were sold in the Temple precincts for the offerings of the purifying (women after childbirth, zavim), and their market price was a live public concern.

label: He quotes Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11
statement: He justified the action by quoting Isaiah 56:7 ('my house shall be called a house of prayer') against Jeremiah 7:11 ('you have made it a den of robbers').

label: The blind and lame healed in the Temple
statement: The blind and the lame came to him in the Temple courts, and he healed them there.

label: Children cry 'Hosanna'; he answers with Psalm 8:2
statement: Children cried 'Hosanna to the son of David' in the Temple, and Jesus answered the indignant chief priests with Psalm 8:2, 'out of the mouth of babes... you have perfected praise'.

label: He lodges at Bethany outside Jerusalem
statement: He left the city each evening and lodged at Bethany, a village outside Jerusalem, during the final week.

label: The leafy fig tree has no fruit and withers at his word
statement: On the morning return he found a roadside fig tree in full leaf but with no fruit, cursed it, and it withered at once.

label: Chief priests and elders question his authority in the Temple
statement: While he was teaching in the Temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people confronted him and demanded by what authority he acted.

label: The leaders fear the crowds because all hold John a prophet
statement: The leaders dared not call John's baptism merely human, because the crowds all held John to be a prophet and the leaders feared them.

label: The two sons and the father's vineyard work
statement: The parable assumes a father's sons owe a day's work in the family vineyard, and that doing the father's will, not the first answer, counts.

label: Vineyard with hedge, winepress and watchtower (Isaiah 5)
statement: The parable's vineyard has a hedge, a dug winepress and a built watchtower, the fittings of Isaiah 5's vineyard song.

label: Absentee landowner leases the vineyard to tenant farmers
statement: The parable assumes an absentee landowner who leases his vineyard to tenant farmers (georgoi) and at harvest sends servants to collect his share of the fruit.

label: He quotes Psalm 118:22-23 (the rejected stone)
statement: He answered with Psalm 118:22-23, the stone the builders rejected made the head of the corner, 'marvelous in our eyes'.

label: The leaders perceive the parables are against them but fear the crowds
statement: The chief priests and Pharisees understood that the parables were spoken against them, and would have seized him but feared the multitudes, who held him to be a prophet.
